newsitem.title: USA: Auto recyclers sue, seek alternative to ADP Inc.
newsitem.headline: Auto recyclers sue, seek alternative to ADP Inc.

text.p: United Recyclers Group LLC, a trade association of automobile recyling businesses, said Tuesday it was seeking relief from an alleged monopoly created by Automated Data Processing, by filing suit against ADP.
The group also said that it is pooling its resources to find an alternative to ADP's management information systems that provide data to the industry.

The group said that the Federal Trade Commission and the firm of Chimicles Jacobsen & Tickellis have both made similar claims, alleging that ADP planned and then executed the plan to "expeditiously" monopolize the electronic data systems that automotive recyclers and auto body shops use.

The group said ADP first acquired one of the recyclers management systems providers in 1992, and acquired the second and only other major provider in May, 1995. United Recycling said the FTC investigated the acquisitions, later fining ADP $2.97 million for violating pre-merger disclosure requirements.
Other industry participants, including body shops, also believe that their services from ADP could be improved or become less expensive, in a pre-merger competitive environment, said the group.
Representatives from ADP were unavalable for comment.
